tldr: Having multiple LLM instances propose, critique, and revise answers over debate rounds reliably beats single-agent generation and self-reflection — e.g. GSM8K 77.0 to 85.0% — and the resulting debate transcripts can be distilled back, creating a model self-improvement loop.
method: Multiple copies of gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 independently answer the same prompt (zero-shot chain-of-thought) — only black-box generations, no weights or likelihoods. Each debate round, every agent receives the other agents' full responses concatenated as context plus a consensus prompt ("using the solutions from other agents as additional information, can you provide your answer?") and revises. Main configuration: 3 agents, 2 rounds; accuracy rises monotonically with agents and rounds (gains plateau past 4 rounds; 5+ agents need peers' responses summarized to fit context). "Stubborn" long-form prompts slow consensus and improve final answers; convergence is not guaranteed (debate is a multi-agent game) but agents almost always settle on one shared answer. Unlike majority voting, the model itself integrates the responses.
results: Arithmetic: 81.8±2.3% vs 67.0±4.7% single agent; self-reflection 72.1%, majority voting only 69.0% (3 agents, 2 rounds)
GSM8K: 85.0±3.5% vs 77.0±4.2% single agent (majority voting 81.0%); helps with and without zero-shot CoT
Chess move optimality (Stockfish pawn-score delta): 122.9±7.6 vs 91.4±10.6 single agent
Factuality: new 524-computer-scientist biography benchmark 73.8±2.3 vs 66.0±2.2; MMLU 71.1±4.6 vs 63.9 single — self-reflection drops MMLU to 57.7; chess move validity 45.2 vs 29.3
chatGPT+Bard debate solves 17/20 GSM8K vs 14 (chatGPT) and 11 (Bard) alone; persona initialization lifts MMLU 71.1 to 74.2
advantages: Makes debate between model copies a practical inference-time gain on black-box APIs: identical prompts and procedure across all six tasks, no gradient or likelihood access
Beats majority voting (the model integrates answers rather than tallying them) and peer critique beats self-reflection — which actually hurt factuality on MMLU (57.7 vs 63.9)

Not just answer amplification: many cases show all agents initially wrong yet converging on the correct answer; agents disagree on uncertain facts and drop them, and ease of persuasion may itself signal factual confidence
Explicitly frames debate transcripts as training data to distill back into the base model — a self-improvement loop — and introduces the biography factuality benchmark
limitations: Computationally expensive: every round needs a full generation per agent, multiplying cost (paper's own §5), though framed as data generation for distillation
Convergence is not correctness: debates settle on single answers that can be wrong while agents confidently affirm them — models cannot express uncertainty, so shared errors survive (§5)
Long debates overflow attention: models "only focused on the most recent generations" of a long debate history
Small eval sets (~100 problems per task) and the biography metric uses chatGPT itself as judge; agents' agreeableness may be an artifact of RLHF instruction tuning
fits: The canonical multi-agent debate paper — the social, quorum-based alternative to single-model self-correction at stage 6. Pairs with the Divergent Thinking paper (2305.19118): that motivates why diverse self-attempts help, this supplies the consensus mechanism later RSI pipelines reuse to generate training data.
reading: Sections 2.1–2.2 (protocol, prompt-controlled consensus), Tables 1–2 with Figure 10 (agents/rounds scaling), and §5 Limitations; Figure 3 plus §3.3 for short vs long debate prompts.
